about: The Fasteners bridge's tools for agents (through Agent Link), listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed: name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

card.does: Reads the types, sizes and lengths of Fasteners Workbench, from its own tables.

kind.means: A kind: screw, nut, washer, insert, pin ...

size.means: A size, written as Fasteners writes it: M3, #10, 1/4in ...

links.line: type and size: the answer holds lengths, hole and insert
With no type, the types that match query, standard and kind

effects: These tools are listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed
There are three levels
With no type: the answer holds the types that match query, standard and kind
With no type: the first 40 types
With type: the answer holds the sizes of that type and hasLength
With type and size: the answer holds lengths, hole and insert
hole: the pass and tap hole diameters from Fasteners' own screw calculator
insert: the hole and depth of an IUT heat-set insert
Changes nothing
Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer
tapHole is the drill for a tapped thread; nominal is the thread's own diameter, not a pass hole.

types.means: Per type: type, kind, what (the first 40)

length.means: { any, default } for one cut to length

hole.means: { tapHole, nominal, units: mm }: tap hole and nominal diameter of the size

insert.means: { hole, depth, outer, insert, source } of the IUT heat-set insert, for IUTHeatInsert

more.means: how many types are not shown

type.means: The Fasteners type name, with one type asked for

kind.means: What kind of fastener the type is, as Fasteners names it

group.means: The group the type is listed in

standard.means: The standard the type belongs to

what.means: Fasteners' one-line help for the type

size.means: The size asked for, when one size of a type is read

source.means: Where the figures come from: Fasteners Workbench

kinds.means: [kind, ...] every kind listed; only when no type matches

standards.means: [standard, ...] every standard listed; only when no type matches

refusalNotes: A type that is not one is refused not_found, with the nearest names
A size that the type does not come in is refused, with the sizes it does
hints: Narrow the query for more types
hw_hole { kind: "clearance" } sizes the pass hole (ISO 273).
Narrow with query, standard or kind when more is given.
fastener_types { type } lists the sizes of a type (a screwNote noSize names the type).

fastener_types.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

card.does: Adds a Fasteners Workbench part (screw, bolt, nut, washer, insert, pin ...).

type.means: The type name of Fasteners, for example ISO4762

size.means: A size such as M3; it wins over the hole

length.means: The nearest length the type comes in

thread.means: simple: a plain cylinder, fast. real: a modelled thread, slow and heavy, for close-ups only

edges.means: Round edges; one fastener is attached to each

at.means: Where the loose fastener goes [x, y, z]; the origin when left out

match.means: outer or inner: the kind of hole the edge is
forms: outer: the edge is a pass hole, and the screw goes through
inner: a tap hole, and its thread fits it

invert.means: true turns it end for end

links.line: Without edges, it is made loose at at
match tells if the edge is a pass hole or a tap hole
Left out on edges, Fasteners matches the size to the diameter of the edge

effects: near is a point on the round edge or at the centre of the hole, within 1 mm
On an edge, the fastener is seated
Seated: its head is on the open side of the edge
The head of a nut or washer is its face; the head of an insert is its top
The shank goes into the material, whichever way FreeCAD's circle for that edge points
Fasteners puts the head where the axis of the circle points
On a PartDesign Hole, that can be into the plate
The shape cannot always tell the open side (a rim with material on both sides)
Then it is as Fasteners places it
A size given on the wall of a counterbore goes on the edge of the bore at its floor
attachNote says so
Kept on its hole: each attached fastener also keeps the geometry of the edge (centre, axis, radius)
A later PartDesign feature can renumber the edges of the Body
The fastener is then put back on the same round edge (reattached)
When no edge of that size is left within reach, it stays where it is and says so
It is then lost, with a Report-view warning
Labels read "M8x25-Screw", "M8x25-Screw 2" ..., numbered per size and kept
Fasteners itself relabels at every recompute
Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer
The answer of a changing call can also hold health from the shared check
At a centre, near takes the nearest centre, then the hole's outer rim

made.means: Per fastener: object, label, type, kind, size, length, matchOuter, offset, edgeDiameter, at, hidden, shankOut, attachNote, reattached, lost, adopted

source.means: Where the fastener data comes from: Fasteners Workbench

made.attachedTo.means: The edge it is on, for example "Plate.Edge7"

made.headSide.means: The open side, or in the material when turned end for end

made.shankOut.means: mm the shank stands out of the hole's far rim: a screw longer than its hole

refusalNotes: Refused: an unknown type (the nearest names are given)
Refused: a size that the type does not come in
Refused: an edge that is not circular
Refused: a point with no round edge within 1 mm (the nearest are listed)
Refused: thread or match other than their two words
hints: Prefer near: edge numbers change after any edit of the body
A lost fastener: fastener_set { edge } puts it on another

fastener_add.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

card.does: Changes Fasteners parts in place, as Fasteners' own Change Parameters, Flip and Move do.

objects.means: Names or labels (fastener_list gives them); required unless only restore

type.means: Only one with the same properties, for example a screw to another screw standard

size.means: "Auto" matches it to its hole again

length.means: The nearest length it comes in

invert.means: true turns it end for end from seated; false seats it

edge.means: Another round edge ("Plate.Edge9"): moves it there, seated

restore.means: true gives the Fasteners objects of the document their behaviour back

label.means: For ONE fastener, the label that it then keeps across recomputes (Fasteners' own relabelling is undone)

links.line: With several objects, label is refused
On a move to another edge, it is turned end for end there only when it was before
On a move to another edge, it is turned end for end there when invert says so

effects: Each part keeps its object name and label
Give any of these inputs
restore alone: the answer holds restored
shankOut is a length longer than the hole, as a 20 mm screw in a 10 mm plate
A changed fastener can still be "not recomputed yet" after its last step, and not before the call
It is then recomputed once more, so the health check of the next call does not list it
Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer
The answer of a changing call can also hold health from the shared check
A restore gives Fasteners saved where Fasteners Workbench was not loaded its proxy back.
With invert true, the head goes into the material
With invert false, the head is on the open side

changed.means: Per fastener: object, label, type, kind, size, length, matchOuter, offset, edgeDiameter, at, hidden, shankOut, attachNote, reattached, lost, adopted

restored.means: the fasteners that got their proxy back (empty when none needed it)

changed.attachedTo.means: The edge it is on, for example "Plate.Edge7"

changed.headSide.means: The open side, or in the material when turned end for end

refusalNotes: Another type is refused, with a list of what it can become
Refused: an object that is not a Fasteners part
Refused: a type that it cannot become, or a size that it does not come in
hints: Use restore when the file was saved where Fasteners Workbench was not loaded

fastener_set.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

card.does: Lists the Fasteners parts in the document and their bill of materials.

sheet.means: true also puts the BOM in a spreadsheet in the document

effects: They are counted from the objects as they are now
Each fastener is listed once, hidden ones too (hidden: true)
The links and arrays of it that Fasteners counts are listed too
Before listing, each attached fastener is checked against its hole
hole kept: on its hole
hole reattached: put back on the same circle after FreeCAD renumbered the edges
hole lost: its hole moved or was removed
A lost fastener is also under warnings
Fasteners from before Workshop kept them are taken in as the document opens or recomputes
They come from older documents, or were added with Fasteners' own buttons
Their hole comes from the edge they are on
A label that Fasteners counted up is put back in the per-size scheme; adopted: true says so
With the window up, the sheet is Fasteners' own Generate BOM; else it is Workshop's, in the same layout
With sheet, the call changes the document, and the answer adds sheet and by
Without sheet, it is a read
The reattaching above is the keeper's own doing, not this call's
Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer
Fasteners' own BOM leaves a hidden fastener out and needs the window
Then Workshop writes the sheet (Type, Qty), which counts the hidden fastener

fasteners.means: Per fastener: object, label, type, kind, size, length, matchOuter, offset, edgeDiameter, at, hidden, attachNote, reattached, lost, adopted

bom.means: Per item: item ("ISO4762 Screw M3x12"), qty

warnings.means: [lost note of each lost fastener: { fastener, reason: objectGone | edgeLost, object, edge, diameter, at, reach }]

sheet.means: The BOM spreadsheet, with sheet: true

by.means: who made the BOM sheet: Fasteners' Generate BOM, or Workshop

hidden.means: up to 3 labels of hidden fasteners that Fasteners' own BOM would leave out

reason.means: needsWindow: the Fasteners BOM command needs the window

source.means: Where the fastener data comes from: Fasteners Workbench

fasteners.attachedTo.means: The edge it is on, for example "Plate.Edge7"

fasteners.headSide.means: The open side, or in the material when turned end for end

hints: fastener_set { edge } puts a lost fastener on another edge
fastener_set { objects: [name], edge } puts a fastener that lost its hole on an edge.

card.does: Reads or sets the 3D-print thread settings of Fasteners Workbench.

nut.means: [A, B] for inside threads (1.03, 0.1 to start); used when mode is 3dprint

screw.means: [A, B] for outside threads (0.99, −0.05); used when mode is 3dprint

links.line: nut and screw apply when mode is 3dprint
Give mode, nut [A, B] and/or screw [A, B] to set them

effects: The settings are Fasteners' own preference, for every document on this computer, and they are not kept with the file
Called with nothing, it only reads the settings
The diameter of a printed thread is d x A + B
After a set, every fastener with a real (modelled) thread in every open document is recomputed and named under redone
This is slow when there are many
When mode is 3dprint, the modelled threads of thread_cut in a printed body take the nut figures as their clearance
history_undo does not undo it: it is a preference, not part of the document
Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer

mode.means: standard or 3dprint: how Fasteners makes threads

nut.means: [A, B]: a printed nut thread's diameter is d x A + B

screw.means: [A, B]: a printed screw thread's diameter is d x A + B

source.means: Where the settings come from: Fasteners Workbench, 3D Print Settings

redone.means: [label of each threaded fastener recomputed after a set]

refusalNotes: Refused: a mode other than the two
Refused: nut or screw that is not two numbers
hints: To undo a set, call it again with the old figures
